title: Acts 11:1–18
context: News reaches Judea that Gentiles have received God’s word, and circumcised believers criticize Peter for eating with uncircumcised men. Peter explains step by step: the vision, the Spirit’s instruction, the angel’s message to Cornelius, and the Spirit falling on the Gentiles as on the apostles at the beginning. If God gave them the same gift, who was Peter to stand in God’s way? The critics fall silent and glorify God, concluding that God has granted the Gentiles repentance to life.

verses.text: Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
verses.arminianNotes: The apostles and brothers hear that Gentiles received the word. Arminian readers see news spreading quickly through the church.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see a turning point in the history of redemption.

verses.text: When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him,
verses.arminianNotes: The circumcision party criticizes Peter. Arminian commentators see sincere believers struggling with change.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see the church needing to submit its traditions to God’s revelation.

verses.text: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!”
verses.arminianNotes: “You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them!” Arminian readers see table fellowship as the heart of the dispute.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the issue of whether Gentiles must become Jews to belong to God.

verses.text: But Peter began, and explained to them in order, saying,
verses.arminianNotes: Peter explains in order. Arminian expositors see patient explanation rather than authority alone.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the church persuaded by God’s acts and word.

verses.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It came as far as me.
verses.arminianNotes: He recounts the vision of the sheet. Arminian readers see personal testimony as persuasive.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see revelation as the basis of the decision.

verses.text: When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.
verses.arminianNotes: He saw all kinds of animals. Arminian commentators see the vision retold faithfully.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see repetition underscoring importance.

verses.text: I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat!’
verses.arminianNotes: He heard, “Rise, Peter, kill and eat!” Arminian readers see Peter admitting his initial resistance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s command preceding understanding.

verses.text: But I said, ‘Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’
verses.arminianNotes: He refused because nothing unclean had entered his mouth. Arminian expositors see Peter identifying with his critics.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see a sincere conscience corrected by God.

verses.text: But a voice answered me the second time out of heaven, ‘What God has cleansed, don’t you call unclean.’
verses.arminianNotes: “What God has cleansed, don’t call unclean.” Arminian readers see the decisive word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s declaration settling the matter.

verses.text: This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.
verses.arminianNotes: It happened three times. Arminian commentators see certainty in repetition.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see God confirming his word.

verses.text: Behold, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.
verses.arminianNotes: Three men arrived at that moment. Arminian readers see timing that points to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see providence coordinating events.

verses.text: The Spirit told me to go with them without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.
verses.arminianNotes: The Spirit told him to go without discriminating, and six brothers came along. Arminian expositors see witnesses who can confirm the story.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the Spirit removing distinctions.

verses.text: He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa and get Simon, who is called Peter,
verses.arminianNotes: Cornelius had seen an angel telling him to send for Peter. Arminian readers see God’s work on both sides.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God preparing hearer and preacher.

verses.text: who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and all your house.’
verses.arminianNotes: Peter would speak words by which he and his household would be saved. Arminian commentators see that even a devout seeker needed the gospel to be saved.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see salvation coming through the word preached, and paedobaptists note the household language.

verses.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.
verses.arminianNotes: The Spirit fell on them as on the apostles at the beginning. Arminian readers see equal treatment of Gentiles.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the same gift showing they belong to the same people.

verses.text: I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, ‘John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’
verses.arminianNotes: Peter remembered Jesus’ word about baptism in the Spirit. Arminian expositors see Scripture recalled to interpret experience.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the promise of 1:5 extended to Gentiles.

verses.text: If then God gave to them the same gift as us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”
verses.arminianNotes: If God gave them the same gift, who was Peter to hinder God? Arminian readers see God accepting those who believed, and Peter refusing to oppose him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s sovereign action that the church must recognize.

verses.text: When they heard these things, they held their peace and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”
verses.arminianNotes: They glorify God: he has granted the Gentiles repentance unto life. Arminian readers see God opening the way of repentance to the Gentiles as a people, making it possible for them to turn.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see repentance described as God’s gift, granted to those he brings to life, a key text for grace preceding human turning.
